title: Record and grade the corpus on jev-1.13 (hosted) and tev1 (local Ollama)
description: jud record / eval / tune on the held-out split, both backends. tev1 decides whether the feature can keep messages on the machine: hosted means agent mail, which carries code, leaves it (see docs/telemetry.md's stance). Report accuracy with interval, ROC AUC, precision and recall at the tuned bar, and the drift between two identical runs.
acceptance_criteria: Numbers appended to docs/studies/system-one-triage.md; a go/no-go against the study's decision criteria (breaks_something recall >= 0.9 on held-out at a precision the operator accepts; tev1 within reach of jev to stay local)

title: Label a field-run mail corpus for the agent-mail rubric, two annotators, held-out split
description: The study's 33 messages come from one repository after the protocol restrained messaging, so only 4 are status reports, and the rubric was written after reading them. Export authored mail (kind=mail) from the field-run repositories (arkanoid, megablast, grimcast, crucible, quern) and the dogfooding run that sent 85 messages, 41 of them status pings. Label needs_action / breaks_something / status_only per the rubric's criteria, with a second annotator on at least a third.
acceptance_criteria: 150+ labelled messages as a jud Cases document; inter-annotator agreement reported per question; a held-out split fixed before any re-tuning

title: pact audit: calibration line for handoff --confidence (model-free)
description: handoff --confidence high|medium|low is self-reported and never measured. Relate each tier to an outcome pact can derive (a later commit fixing the same paths within N hours, or the dependent bead reopened) and report the rate per tier. A count, never a verdict, like the handoff-coverage line. Needs no model and no judgment dependency.
acceptance_criteria: audit prints per-tier outcome rates with counts; --json carries them; no check fails on it

title: Document the composition recipe: pact msg --json piped to jud, outside pact
description: If the corpus run says go: a fleet-patterns section (or docs/mcp.md, for an MCP triage agent) showing the read-side recipe with no code in pact. Ranks and escalates; never filters. Names the egress trade-off.
acceptance_criteria: Recipe runs end to end on a fixture inbox; check-docs green

title: System One triage of agent mail: follow-ups from the study
description: Follow-ups from docs/studies/system-one-triage.md. The study found one place a calibrated verdict helps pact: ranking authored mail by what it needs from its reader (needs_action, breaks_something, status_only), read side only, never hiding a message. Measured on pact's own 33 messages against jev-1.13.0: ranks well (ROC AUC 0.89-0.97), thresholds badly at 0.5. Everything here is gated on a larger labelled corpus.

title: Design spike: optional judge feature for pact ui / doctor (rank, and alarm on unread warnings)
description: Only after the corpus run proves value. Constraints the study set: no default feature; never on msg inbox's hot path uncached; never sets an exit code or gates a command; never hides a message; verdicts cached by message id (content-derived, so stable) and reproducible from recordings; link judgment with --no-default-features and a blocking transport (the otel precedent) rather than shelling out to jud (the bd lesson). doctor alarm = verdict AND recorded fact (unread for N minutes), the fleet-liveness shape.
acceptance_criteria: A decision record: build it or not, with the dependency and binary-size cost measured
